name: Rolen Depot Work Shirt (Patched)
description: A faded grey-green button-up work shirt, originally issued by Rolen Depot to warehouse staff, now three owners and a hundred washes removed from new. The left elbow has been patched twice with mismatched brown synth-canvas; two buttons are replacements in a slightly wrong shade. Collar is frayed but structurally intact.
functionality: Durable long-sleeve coverage with chest pocket; holds up to daily labor and acid-light drizzle.
what_it_says: You work, you survive, you don't waste anything that still has life in it.
story_hooks: The previous owner's name — 'SULLY' — is still written in permanent marker inside the collar.
A folded scrap of paper tucked in the chest pocket contains half a map to somewhere.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn, oversized button-up shirt with a utilitarian silhouette. The fabric hangs loosely from the shoulders with a slightly boxy cut that reads as deliberately slouched rather than tailored. The muted grey-green base is interrupted by visible repair work, giving it a layered, repurposed aesthetic.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and generous through the shoulders and chest; sleeves sit slightly long at the wrist. Designed for movement and durability rather than form-fitting.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-weight cotton-synth blend, original Rolen Depot industrial stock — durable but not high-spec. Patched sections use recycled brown synth-canvas with visible stitching.
physical_description.texture: Soft, heavily worn fabric with a slight nap from repeated washing. Elbow patches are noticeably stiffer and textured against the body of the shirt. Fraying at the collar creates subtle, organic irregularity.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded grey-green as primary; two contrasting brown patch repairs on left elbow; replacement buttons in slightly lighter grey creating subtle tonal breaks down the front.
physical_description.closures: Seven button front, with two replacement buttons (slightly mismatched shade) visible at mid-chest and waist. Original buttons show wear and patina.
distinctive_features: Dual-patched left elbow with visible cross-stitching in darker thread
Frayed collar edges showing fabric history
Visible replacement buttons in wrong shade
Ghost of original Rolen Depot laundry marking barely visible on interior placket
Slight permanent creasing at elbow bends from repetitive wear
Unraveling seam starting at left shoulder
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 working class, edging into Tier 5 salvage culture adoption
physical_description.cultural_context: Originally depot/warehouse, now signals street authenticity and maker culture. Wearing it suggests honest work history, or deliberate adoption of sub-grade aesthetics by someone who can afford better. Common among dock workers, recyclers, and off-grid technicians.
physical_description.condition_typical: Visibly patched and weathered; expected to be worn open over a base layer or as standalone. Never pristine; always appears like it's just come from a shift.
